guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not treating Wake Forest’s 38-16 win over Akron as proof that its offense will translate against Miami, but the debut offered useful context. Wake produced 559 yards, and Gio Lopez threw for 350 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. That showed us an offense capable of creating explosive production without giving away possessions.

The more important part is the step up in resistance. Our matchup data grades Miami among the top 20 in both rush and pass EPA defense and fourth in preventing scoring opportunities, while Wake’s offense sits closer to the middle of the national distribution. The market is asking whether Wake can sustain enough drives against a defense built to prevent exactly that, and our numbers do not dismiss that concern.

We can still see a path to Wake remaining competitive enough, particularly after its 2025 defense finished in the ACC’s top five in total defense and pass defense while holding seven opponents to 14 points or fewer. That history provides some defensive foundation, but it does not create a meaningful enough difference from the market for us at the available price. For us, this remains a pass.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Wake’s passing offense against Miami’s pass defense. Lopez already knows offensive coordinator Rob Ezell from their time together at South Alabama, and Wake allowed no sacks in its opener. The question for us is whether that comfort and protection carry over against a pass defense our data rates far more highly than Wake’s first opponent. If Wake cannot create efficient completions and reach scoring range consistently, staying within the market’s expectation becomes much more difficult.

recent_game.fact: Wake Forest opened the 2026 season with a 38-16 home victory over Akron on Sept. 3.
Wake Forest produced 559 total yards against Akron, including 356 passing yards and 203 rushing yards.
Wake Forest allowed 305 total yards against Akron: 149 rushing and 156 passing.
Wake Forest converted 7 of 15 third downs, went 2-for-2 on fourth down and committed no turnovers against Akron.

quarterback.fact: North Carolina transfer Gio Lopez is Wake Forest's starting quarterback and one of six team captains.
In his Wake Forest debut against Akron, Lopez completed 21 of 32 passes for 350 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing seven times for 39 yards.
Lopez's 78-yard touchdown pass to Carlos Hernandez against Akron was the longest completion of Lopez's college career.
Lopez previously played under current Wake Forest offensive coordinator Rob Ezell at South Alabama.
Wake Forest's unofficial depth chart lists redshirt freshman Steele Pizzella as Lopez's backup.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running back Ty Clark III rushed seven times for a career-high 105 yards against Akron, including a career-long 57-yard run.
Wide receiver Carlos Hernandez caught five passes for 165 yards and a touchdown against Akron and added 18 punt-return yards.
Hernandez has caught at least five passes in each of his last five games, averaging 107.6 receiving yards with five touchdowns over that span.
Wake Forest's unofficial starting receiver group is Carlos Hernandez, Antonio Meeks and Kam Shanks, with Ty Clark III listed as the starting running back.
Wide receiver Ny Carr joined Wake Forest after previously playing at Miami.

defensive_personnel.fact: Wake Forest's six captains include defensive end Langston Hardy, linebacker Aiden Hall and defensive back Davaughn Patterson.
The unofficial defensive depth chart lists Langston Hardy and Gabe Kirschke at defensive end, Dallas Afalava at defensive tackle and Zach Lohavichan at nose guard.
